item.content:encoded:
The bottleneck for investment research Agents isn't the model, it's data governance and human judgment; using overseas models will make you dumber, using domestic models forces you to get smarter.

An FDE who has pushed AI investment research to its limits explains the real bottlenecks of Agent deployment, the pitfalls of multi-Agent collaboration, and why AI still can't do long-cycle judgment.

6:06 Agent projects get stuck on data, not on the Agent
Lao Bai says a large number of AI Agent project deliveries get stuck not on the Agent, but on data. To solve problems you have to hunt for data everywhere, and much of it sits on different platforms with different specs and types. Many websites have anti-scraping mechanisms, so web search can't reach them; a single website might have tens of thousands or even hundreds of thousands of pages, and figuring out which page is actually useful is very hard. He believes data governance will be the most important core of getting AI Agent projects to land, even more than 50%. On the logic level, capabilities improved substantially after K3 came out, and the problems and solutions seen day to day are basically covered.

13:10 Using someone else's Agent gives you a product manager's thinking
Lao Bai says if you use your own Agent, its training forms internal memory files through your conversations with it, and the answers it gives you are your mirror. But if you use an Agent that has been trained and you can't train it, then that's the product manager's thinking, not yours. Every AI investment research terminal on the market, whether Walk or Claw, is largely hard-coded by product managers, and users find it very hard to further train such Agents. To get a style that suits you, you must find an AI Agent platform with an open底层 to train it.

18:11 The pitfall of multi-Agent collaboration: calling a skill without its underlying files
Lao Bai points out that interactions between multi-Agent platforms have many pitfalls to avoid. For example, when you call another Agent's skill through one Agent, the result differs from when the Agent that owns the skill calls it. The reason is that when you call another Agent's skill from one Agent, that skill doesn't call the underlying files inside the Agent it belongs to when it executes — equivalent to all your Agent training having no effect underneath, just handing the skill's capability to the current Agent. So multi-Agent collaboration has a certain threshold, and that's the value of an FDE.

24:13 Codex and Claude Code are for writing code, not for investment research
Lao Bai stresses that Codex and Claude Code are products of Web Coding, not Web Walking. For example, SuperPower is a very famous plugin on Claude Code — brainstorm first, then write a report according to a plan, then check it, very perfect — but this thing is actually not suitable for investment research; it's for Coding, for breaking a problem into a project, writing it as code, and delivering it, not for producing research reports. Workbody is an office platform for Workspace Agents, not an investment research platform. FanBot is the multi-Agent platform for investment research.

25:14 Using overseas models will make you dumber
Lao Bai says he talked with a public fund manager yesterday and they agreed: using overseas models will make you dumber, using domestic models will make you smarter. Because overseas models are too smart, you don't need to be very smart; but with domestic models you really do need to be smarter, otherwise the results are unsatisfactory. He explains why he has always stuck with domestic models: using overseas models feels great, so you'll keep using them and won't spend as much time thinking. There's a theory overseas called AI will make the brain degenerate — like lying in bed for 20 days, can you still walk normally when you get up?

45:18 Curing AI laziness: delete memory first, add checks last
Lao Bai says AI is very lazy, because it wants to use the fastest way to tell you the best answer, so it makes things up for you. He gives a real scenario: a dozen years ago a classmate was deputy general manager of a property company, and his biggest pain was no one patrolling at midnight; later they put notebooks in various places in the building, and the security guard would sign in at each point every day, and a round took exactly two hours. AI is the same. The first step of his Harness is to delete all memory, so it can't use historical data to fool you; the last step is to add a layer of data checking. This is exactly the same as the workflow SuperPower designs — the head and tail greatly reduce the hallucination rate.

58:24 Agents won't make ordinary people excellent
Lao Bai concludes: an Agent won't make an ordinary person particularly excellent, but it will make an excellent person particularly excellent. Because the Agent itself has many thresholds and demands on people. He gives an example from three years ago: a person tells AI to make me a Taobao website — this was a famous joke at the time. But in the first half of this year he talked with someone who had used Claude Code for a long time and used many overseas models, and that person still asked questions in exactly that way when using AI, and the result must have been terrible. So AI actually has a threshold for a person's ability.

1:13:32 Long-term re-growth test: AI predicts storage capacity expansion
Lao Bai shares a scenario where AI is irreplaceable. He has a dedicated skill called long-term re-growth test, with a growth-stock-oriented framework, requiring T+2 greater than T+1. In May and June this year he used this skill to look at four industries: storage, real estate, Chinese baijiu. At the time it appeared for one day on Feb5, he asked the question, and by the afternoon it was no longer available. AI's judgment was very clear: under 70% to 80% gross margin and 60% net margin, supply-side discipline means Micron, Samsung, and Hynix will definitely expand capacity, and it even mentioned which plants will come online in 27, and said more expansion plans would be visible in Q3 and Q4 this year. Lao Bai says even an investment manager who has long watched storage would find it hard to collect this data or reach the same granularity.
